title: Trans–New Guinea languages - Wikipedia
text: Trans–New Guinea (TNG) is an extensive family of Papuan languages spoken on the island of New Guinea and neighboring islands, a region corresponding to the country Papua New Guinea as well as parts of Indonesia.

title: Utarmbung language - Wikipedia
text: Osum, also known as Utarmbung, is a divergent Madang language of the Adelbert Range of Papua New Guinea.

title: Utarmbung Language (OMO) – L1 & L2 Speakers, Status, Map ...
text: Utarmbung is a stable indigenous language of Papua New Guinea. It belongs to the Trans-New Guinea language family. Direct evidence is lacking, but the language is thought to be used as a first language by all in the ethnic community. It is not known to be taught in schools.

title: Utarmbung language — Grokipedia
text: Utarmbung, also known as Osum, is classified as a Trans-New Guinea language within the Madang branch, specifically belonging to the Southern Adelbert subgroup of the Adelbert Range languages in Papua New Guinea.
